prerequisite: what a computer program that learns from examples is

must_cover.point: What an LLM is in simple terms: a computer program trained on a very large amount of text that writes text by predicting the next word (token).
Training: the model learns patterns from training data by guessing the next word many billions of times; the numbers it adjusts are called parameters.
Tokens: text is broken into small pieces called tokens before the model reads it.
Prompting: you give the model a prompt, and it predicts a reply one token at a time.
Why LLMs matter: they can explain, summarise, translate and draft text in many languages, which helps learning and work.
Limits: knowledge cutoff (no knowledge of events after training), hallucination (confident wrong answers), and no real understanding or memory of you between chats unless a product adds it.
At least one realistic use case (for example: explaining a hard textbook topic, translating a notice, or drafting an email).

facts: An LLM predicts the next token based on patterns in its training data.
Training data is a very large collection of text, such as books and web pages.
Parameters are numbers inside the model that are adjusted during training.
A token is a small piece of text: a word or part of a word.
An LLM has a knowledge cutoff: it does not know about events after its training data ends.
LLMs can hallucinate: produce fluent text that is false.
An LLM does not look up facts in a database while answering, unless a tool or system is added to it.
Checking important answers against a trusted source is good practice.

misconceptions.wrong: An LLM understands and thinks exactly like a human.
misconceptions.right: It predicts likely text from patterns; it does not think like a person.

misconceptions.wrong: An LLM searches the internet for every answer.
misconceptions.right: On its own it answers from patterns learned in training; search only happens if a tool is added.

misconceptions.wrong: Everything an LLM says is true.
misconceptions.right: It can confidently produce false answers (hallucinations).

misconceptions.wrong: An LLM keeps learning from every chat it has with you.
misconceptions.right: Its parameters do not change while you chat; training happens before release.

misconceptions.wrong: An LLM stores a copy of every book it was trained on and reads from it.
misconceptions.right: It stores learned patterns in its parameters, not a library of documents.
